key: The primary key is your Aadhaar number
name: ch03_id_card_voter_list
alt: One ID card points to exactly one person, while a voter list sorted by street groups many residents under each street.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a large national ID card held up in the hand of a smiling middle-aged woman in a cotton salwar suit; the card shows a small photo, a long number in big digits, and a single bold arrow runs from the number to her alone, with a green tick, to show one number always means exactly one person. Behind her, a queue of other people each hold their own different card, every card pointing only to its owner. RIGHT panel: the wall of a village panchayat office where a printed voter list is pinned on a notice board, sorted by street; a retired schoolteacher in a white kurta and spectacles runs his finger down it. The sheet is drawn in two halves: the upper half has a bold street heading with several resident names grouped beneath it, many people under one street; the lower half shows the same people written as one line each, every line starting with the street and a house number so no two lines are alike. Curved arrows go from one street heading to four little house icons. A calendar on the wall shows a single year circled, hinting the list is printed once a year. Calm morning light, orderly mood. Labels: "PRIMARY KEY" above the left panel, "SECONDARY INDEX" above the right panel.

key: order log is the fact table: each line says
name: ch03_order_slip_star_schema
alt: A long food-delivery order log in the centre with arrows out to the menu, restaurant list, customer list, coupon book and calendar, and the restaurant list pointing on to a cuisines card.
scene: A top-down view of a large office table at a food-delivery company, arranged like a star. In the exact centre lies a long paper roll of order lines, each line a row of small numbered boxes with a tiny rupee coin at its end, unrolling towards the viewer; a young operations analyst in a hoodie leans over it with a highlighter. Around the roll sit five smaller objects, each linked to the roll by a straight arrow from one column of the order lines: at the top a folded restaurant menu card with a bowl of biryani on it (what was ordered), at the upper right a clipboard list of restaurants with tiny shop-front icons (where), at the lower right a contact card stack with little face icons (who), at the lower left a booklet of tear-off coupons (why it was cheap), and at the upper left a wall calendar with an oil lamp drawn on one festival date (when). From the restaurant clipboard, one more short arrow leads outward to a small separate card showing a few cuisine icons, a curry bowl, a dosa and noodles, so that the restaurant list points to it instead of repeating it. Bright, even office light, tidy and organised mood. Labels: "FACT TABLE" along the central order roll, "DIMENSIONS" near the top edge above the ring of objects, "SNOWFLAKE" next to the small cuisines card.

key: A class attendance sheet: one row per student
name: ch03_attendance_bitmaps
alt: A teacher lays two day columns of an attendance sheet side by side to find who came on either day or on both, while a long absence is summed up as a few counts.
scene: A primary-school classroom at the end of the day, seen from the front. A young teacher in a sari and a cardigan stands at her desk with a large attendance sheet: one row per student, one column of tick boxes per day. She has cut two day columns out as long paper strips and laid them side by side on the desk; in the LEFT part of the picture, a third strip below them shows the result where a row is ticked if either strip has a tick, many ticks, and a little blackboard beside it reads one short word. In the CENTRE, she lays a day strip next to a green strip for the cricket team and a result strip below shows ticks only on the rows where both are ticked, just two ticks, with a small cricket bat icon. On the RIGHT, a long row of empty boxes for one sick student, with a few ticks in the middle, is squeezed into a small speech bubble from the teacher that simply shows three numbers, 14, 3 and 9, beside little cross and tick icons, while the long row itself is folded up like an accordion. A boy with a school bag watches, impressed. Chalk dust in warm afternoon light, calm mood. Labels: "OR" above the first result strip, "AND" above the second result strip, "RUN-LENGTH" above the speech bubble.

key: A stack of exam answer sheets sorted by class first
name: ch03_answer_sheets_sort_order
alt: A tall stack of answer sheets sorted by class forms three big coloured blocks that an exam clerk sums up in three short lines, while roll numbers form shorter runs and marks look random.
scene: An exam cell office after board exams, seen from the side. A tall stack of answer sheets stands on a wooden table; each sheet has a coloured class band on its edge, and because the stack is sorted by class first, the edge shows three big solid blocks of colour, teal, amber and plum, one block per class, like a striped cake. Next to the stack, an exam clerk in his 30s in a checked shirt and spectacles writes on a small notepad just three short lines, one per colour block, each with a coloured swatch and a count, "7A x40", "7B x38", "7C x41", with a curved arrow from each block to its line, showing three lines describe the whole column. Beside the stack, a narrow strip of paper shows the roll numbers in the same order: they climb 1, 2, 3 and then restart at 1 at each colour change, drawn as three short rising staircases. A second strip shows the marks column as a jumble of scattered dots with no pattern, and a little question mark over it. A ceiling fan, a steel cupboard and a bundle of string sit in the background. Bright tube light, methodical mood. Labels: "SORTED BY CLASS" above the stack, "3 LINES" next to the notepad.

key: A cricket scorecard. The ball-by-ball log is the raw fact table
name: ch03_scorecard_data_cube
alt: A fan reads a batter's runs straight off the scorecard, but a question about fast balls sends the scorer back to the long ball-by-ball log.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a cricket ground's scorer box, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a big printed scorecard grid on the wall, rows for batters, columns for overs, with neat totals along the edges; a young fan in a team jersey and a cap points at one total and grins, a quick green tick beside it, because the answer is ready to read. RIGHT panel: the same fan now asks a second question shown in a speech bubble with a small speed-gun icon and the short text "140 km/h"; the scorecard behind has a red question mark, because it has no column for ball speed. Instead, the elderly scorer, a man in his 60s with a white cap and reading glasses, unrolls a very long paper scroll on the desk, one line per ball, each line with small icons for bowler, batter, runs and a speed reading, and runs his finger down it line by line, the scroll spilling off the desk and onto the floor. A curved arrow in the background runs from the scroll up to the scorecard, showing the card was built from the scroll. Late afternoon stadium light through the window, floodlight towers outside. Labels: "DATA CUBE" above the scorecard, "FACT TABLE" above the long scroll.
